tutoIntro: The schedule reads your Google Calendar: one calendar entry = one stream. Here is where to write each piece of information.
tutoColWhere: Where to write it in Google Calendar
tutoColDoes: What the schedule does with it
tutoTitleDoes: Shown as is as the stream title. Do not put the game name there: the game is never guessed from the title.
tutoWhenDoes: Shown in {tz} time (the module's “Time zone” setting).
tutoEndDoes: Used to know when the stream is over (it then leaves the schedule) and to show “Happening now” while it runs.
tutoGameWhere: In the description: a line starting with “Game:” followed by the game name
tutoGameDoes: Shows the game name and its cover art. Several games: “Game: Celeste, Hades” or “Game: Celeste + Hades” (3 at most). No “Game:” line = no game: the site logo is shown instead of cover art.
tutoDescDoes: Ignored: only the “Game:” line is read. You can keep notes for yourself there.
tutoPlaceDoes: Not read by the schedule: no need to fill it in.
tutoAllDayDoes: Shown as “All day”, with no time, game or cover art. Avoid it for a stream: give a start and end time instead.
tutoRepeatDoes: Each occurrence appears in the schedule. Editing “this event only” changes a single date.
tutoCancelWhere: Delete the event (or “this event only” for a repeating one)
tutoCancelDoes: It leaves the schedule at the next reload.
tutoStep1: On a computer, open Google Calendar (these settings are not in the mobile app).
tutoStep2: Recommended: create a calendar just for streams (“Other calendars” → “+” → “Create new calendar”). Everything in it becomes visible on the site.
tutoStep3: Gear icon → “Settings”, then click the calendar's name in the left column.
tutoStep4: Scroll to “Integrate calendar” and copy “Secret address in iCal format”. You do not need to make the calendar public.
tutoStep5: Paste it in the “Calendar address” setting above, then save. Share it with nobody: whoever has it can read the calendar.
tutoExNoGameTitle: Same for an event without a game (charity, chat…): simply write no “Game:” line.
tutoErr1: The address is refused or unreadable: copy the full “secret” address (it starts with https:// and ends with .ics). If you reset the address in Google, paste the new one.
tutoErr2: Times are off: set the module's “Time zone” (e.g. Europe/Paris); the default is UTC.
tutoErr3: The game does not show: the line must start with “Game:” in the description (not in the title); check the spelling for the cover art.
tutoErr4: A stream entered as “all day” has no time or cover art: untick the box and enter the times.
tutoErr5: A change does not show right away: Google updates the calendar with a delay and the module keeps it 5 minutes in memory. “Refresh now” reloads on the site's side.
skillBtn: Download the skill for my AI
skillHelp: A SKILL.md file to give your AI assistant (Claude, etc.): it learns to fill your calendar the way the schedule expects. It contains no secret.
skillDesc: Creates, edits or cancels Google Calendar events in the format read by the stream schedule of {site} (title, “Game:” line, times in {tz}). Use whenever asked to add or change a stream in the calendar.
skillBody:
# Filling the stream schedule calendar of {site}

## Role

You fill in the Google Calendar that the stream schedule of {site} is built from. Every event in that calendar becomes a stream shown on the site. The schedule reads the calendar as is: any deviation from the format changes what visitors see.

## When to use

When asked to add, move, repeat or cancel a stream, a night or an event in the schedule calendar.

## Filling rules (exact)

- **Title**: the stream's name, short, as it should be displayed (e.g. "Discovery night"). The game name is not required in the title; the schedule never guesses the game from the title.
- **Start date and time**: a real start time, in the **{tz}** time zone (the schedule's time zone). Never enter a time without knowing which time zone it is expressed in.
- **Duration**: fill in the end time (default 2 h if the human said nothing, and tell them). The stream leaves the schedule once finished.
- **Game**: in the **description**, a line starting with `Game: ` followed by the exact game name (`Game: Celeste`). Several games: `Game: Celeste, Hades` or `Game: Celeste + Hades` (3 at most). Use the game's usual name (cover art is searched with it).
- **Event without a game** (charity, chat, announcement…): write **no** `Game:` line. The site will show its logo instead of cover art. Never write `Game: none`, `Game: -` or an invented game.
- **Rest of the description**: free, ignored by the schedule (notes for the human).
- **Location**: not read by the schedule; leave it empty.
- **All day**: avoid it for a stream (no time or cover art is shown). Only use it if the human explicitly asks.
- **Repeat**: if the stream comes back every week, use the calendar's repeat (a single entry); edit "this event only" for one particular date.
- **Cancellation**: delete the event (or only that occurrence of a repeating one). Do not rename it "cancelled": it would stay displayed.

## Entry template

```
Title:       <stream name>
Start:       <weekday> <date>, <HH:MM> ({tz})
End:         <weekday> <date>, <HH:MM> ({tz})
Location:    (empty)
Description: Game: <game name>        (no such line if there is no game)
Repeat:      <none | every week …>
```

## Examples

**Gaming stream**

```
Title:       Discovery night
Start:       Saturday 10 October, 21:00 ({tz})
End:         Saturday 10 October, 23:30 ({tz})
Description: Game: Celeste
```

**Charity event, no game**

```
Title:       Cap48h: charity stream
Start:       Saturday 17 October, 14:00 ({tz})
End:         Sunday 18 October, 14:00 ({tz})
Description: Thank you all for your generosity!
```

(no `Game:` line)

**Repeating stream**

```
Title:       Chill Thursday
Start:       Thursday 15 October, 20:30 ({tz})
End:         Thursday 15 October, 22:30 ({tz})
Description: Game: Hades, Celeste
Repeat:      every week, on Thursday
```

## Checklist before creating

1. The title is clear and has no invented game name.
2. Both start AND end times are filled in, in the {tz} time zone.
3. The `Game:` line only exists if a game is really known, and starts the line.
4. "All day" is not ticked (unless explicitly requested).
5. The location is empty.
6. The repeat matches the request.
7. You reviewed the summary with the human for any important change.

## Never do

- Invent or guess a game, a date, a time or a duration.
- Enter a time without a time zone, or in a time zone other than {tz} without converting.
- Write the game in the title or location expecting it to be read.
- Create a duplicate of an existing event: search the calendar first.
- Ask for or copy the calendar's secret address: you do not need it.

## Ask the human when information is missing

- Which day and what time does the stream start, and until when?
- Is there a game? Which one (exact name)? If not, it is an event without a game.
- Is it a recurring slot (every week…) or a single date?
- Should an existing event be replaced?

Ask these in one go, briefly, then create the event and recap the result: title, date, start and end times ({tz}), game or "no game".
